issue.close_reason: Implemented lib/common.sh inlining during installation. Modified install.sh to inline lib/common.sh content into scripts that source it, making installed copies self-contained. issue.description:
Found 2026-08-20 while installing plan-review 2.0. The in-progress lib extraction (uncommitted WIP in plan-author/plan-review/readme-review/spec-review scripts, untracked lib/common.sh) has each script do: source "$(dirname "$0")/../../lib/common.sh". Correct inside the repo, but once a skill is installed to ~/.claude/skills/<skill>/ that path resolves to ~/.claude/lib/common.sh. install.sh copies only the skill directory, so every refactored script fails at its source line with 'No such file or directory' (verified: installed plan-review/scripts/scan-headers.sh exits 1). The parent bead's own spec prescribes that exact path, so the defect is in the spec, not just the WIP.

Options: (a) install.sh also installs lib/ to ~/.claude/skills/lib/ — only works if repo skills and installed skills share the same relative layout; (b) guard the source with an inline fallback — defeats most of the dedup; (c) inline lib/common.sh into each script at install time (a tiny build step in install.sh) — repo stays DRY, installed copies stay self-contained. Recommended: (c). Acceptance: plan-review's SELF-TEST fixture and scan-headers.sh run green from the INSTALLED path, and scripts/check-installed.sh reports no drift.

Until fixed, the installed plan-review carries the HEAD (self-contained) scan-headers.sh and score-plan.sh, so check-installed.sh reports drift on those two files by design.
issue.title: install.sh: scripts that source ../../lib/common.sh break once installed (lib/ not copied)

issue.description:
README.md's install instructions are: clone the whole repo directly into ~/.claude/skills/, or
manually `cp -r <skill> ~/.claude/skills/` one at a time. The first option assumes an empty or

other sources (bd-to-br-migration, beads-overview, claude-status, find-stubs, gap-review,
generate-image, new-repo) plus 2 already installed from this repo (plan-review, repo-hygiene);
cloning this repo directly over that directory would collide/fail.

Add scripts/install.sh (or root install.sh) supporting:
  ./install.sh <skill-name> [<skill-name>...]   # install just these skills
  ./install.sh --all                             # install every skill in this repo
Both modes copy into ~/.claude/skills/<skill>/ without touching any other directory already
there, and print a clear "already installed, overwriting" notice (not a silent clobber) when a
target skill directory already exists. Update README.md's Installation section to lead with
this script instead of the raw `git clone .../.claude/skills` command.

Related: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (follow-on work list).

issue.description:
README's documented remedy for drift is a manual `cp -r plan-review/ ~/.claude/skills/`. After jedscura-abeab37c extracts lib/common.sh and skill scripts source ../../lib/common.sh, copying a single skill directory installs scripts whose lib path resolves outside the copy — the same breakage jedscura-2c6e3560 tracks for install.sh, but in the manual documented workflow, which that bead does not cover. Update the README fix instructions (and any remedy text check-installed.sh prints) to copy lib/ alongside the skill, or replace the manual cp with a documented sync command / install.sh flag that also handles lib/ and the usage-statusline out-of-tree file.

issue.description:
README documents check-installed.sh's exit-code contract (0 = no drift, 1 = drift detected, 2 = usage error or missing ~/.claude/skills/) and install.sh's behavior (--list, selective non-destructive install that doesn't touch other installed skills, --all). No open bead verifies either contract: the ADR-1 harness (jedscura-be4baf66) validates skill bundles, not the repo's own root scripts. Add a fixture-based shell test (temp HOME with a fake ~/.claude/skills/) covering clean tree → 0, drifted/missing file → 1, absent skills dir → 2, and install.sh selective install leaving sibling skills untouched. Wire it alongside validate-skills.sh so these documented contracts cannot silently change.
